lookForward.fits: Berlin Marathon day: Sunday 27 September 2026, start 8:30, about 55,000 runners; the leaders finish around 10:30.
lookForward.headline: Today is marathon Sunday in Berlin
lookForward.line: From 8:30, 55,000 people run 42 kilometres through the city; the fastest finish at the Brandenburg Gate just after ten. The route is closed to cars, the U-Bahn and S-Bahn run as usual. Go, clap for strangers, stay for the slow ones.

funFact.statement: More marathon world records have been set in Berlin than anywhere else.
funFact.reveal: Thirteen. Flat, wide streets, cool late-September air, and a course that barely climbs 40 metres. Chicago is second with seven.

calmRead.fits: Expands the day's look-forward: why the Berlin Marathon, run today, is the fastest in the world.
calmRead.title: Why the world runs fastest in Berlin
calmRead.teaser: Thirteen world records on one course. It is not luck, and it is not only the runners.
paragraphs: At half past eight this morning, 55,000 people set off from the Straße des 17. Juni, and somewhere near the front a small group will be trying to run 42 kilometres faster than any human has before. They chose Berlin for a reason. Thirteen marathon world records have been set here, more than on any other course. Chicago, in second place, has seven.

The first reason is the ground. Berlin is flat. The whole route climbs and falls by about forty metres, less than a walk up a few flights of stairs spread across two hours. The streets are wide, the corners are gentle, and the surface is smooth asphalt almost all the way.
The second is the date. The last Sunday of September in Berlin is usually cool, dry and still. Marathon runners lose their speed in heat, and Berlin gives them ten or twelve degrees at the start.

The third is the crowd. A million people line the route, and they do not go quiet when the leaders have passed. The runners who finish at five hours get the same noise as the runners who finish at two.
The route ends through the Brandenburg Gate, with about 400 metres still to go. Runners say the gate is the hardest part: you can see the finish, and it does not get closer. Then it does.

kindness.text: Go and clap for people you do not know today. Stay for the ones at the back. They need it most.

joke.setup: Why did the marathon runner refuse to stop for a coffee?
joke.punchline: She was on a roll and had no time to espresso herself.

riddle.riddle: Everyone here started in the same place, nobody ends at the same time, and the last to arrive gets the loudest cheer. What is it?
